usageNotes: Use this to read the current cluster-wide firewall configuration before making changes or auditing security posture. Requires Sys.Audit on / — available to API tokens with that privilege. A response showing 'enable': 0 means the firewall is globally disabled regardless of any node- or VM-level rules.
tips: If 'enable' is 0 (or absent, since default is 0), all firewall rules across the cluster are inactive — node and VM rules do nothing until this is set to 1.
ebtables defaults to enabled (1); disabling it removes layer-2 bridging rules cluster-wide, which can expose VM traffic on the same bridge.
log_ratelimit is returned as a formatted string (e.g., '1,burst=5,rate=1/second'); parse it carefully if evaluating log volume.
policy_in/policy_out/policy_forward may be absent from the response if they have never been explicitly set — treat absence as no default-drop safety net.
